Section 34, T21N, R59E.  North side of large unnamed canyon on the west side of Central Butte Mountains, 32 km north of US Highway Rt. 50 on the Long Valley Road, Butte Mountains, White Pine County.
stratcomments: 105' (32 m) below top of Arcturus Group.
lithdescript: The rocks containing this community are calcareous mudstone and siltstone and wackestones with a high proportion of clay and noncalcaroues silt.  The community is sometimes found in coarser grained muddy sandstone and packstone.  The sediments are thin bedded and sometimes laminated.
collectors: T. Yancey, L. Plas, M. Kaasa
collection_comments: Also included is 500 ostracod (indiv.) and 1 pentacrinoid (indiv.)

geogcomments: Section 34, T. 16 N., R. 62 E. North side of Murry Summit, along Nevada Highway Rt. 6, at the north end of Ward Mountain, 10 kilometers (6 miles) SW of Ely, Nevada. Egan Range, White Pine County, Nevada.
stratcomments: 240' (73 m) above base of Loray Fm.
lithdescript: The enclosing rock consists of wackestone and packstone that was a sediment of mud or muddy sand, containing a small to moderate amount of clay and noncalcareous silt.  The beds are separated by thin, clayey shale partings and are interbedded with noncarbonate strata.  The coarse component consists of shell material that is broken, abraded, and sometimes well-rounded.
collectors: T. Yancey, L. Plas, M. Kaasa
taxonomy_comments: Also included in the list are: 1 demosponge indiv., 5 encrusting bryozoan forms, 1 ramose form, 15 fenestellid forms, 420 undetermined molluscs, 2 crinoids, and 2 echinoids.

geogcomments: 5003-km distance marker on the Sino-Nepal Highway. About 2 km north of Zhongbei. Entire exposure is ~100m wide and ~20 m high.
stratcomments: Fossils come from a Permian exotic block within undifferentiated Triassic rocks. It is one of a group of isolated blocks in the so-called Zhongbei melange of the North Yarlungzangbo melange subbelt (Wang et al, 1996).
lithdescript: Mainly reddish densely-fissured crinoidal limestone; the uppermost part of the carbonate sequence of Sheng (1984). No internal stratigraphy was observed.
geology_comments: This is interpreted as an isolated block most likely representing an isolated seamount or a Permian carbonate platform located on the outer shelf of the southern margin in the Neotethys. It probably collided with and became sandwiched into younger marine deposits during the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates during the early Cenozoic.

Fauna from the Esino Limestone of Val Parina (Val Brembana, Bergamo) in the Southern Alps of Val Parina, a lateral valley of Val Brembana, is located about 30 km north of Bergamo (northern Italy). Outcrops scattered along a gully and on its eastern ridge from 550m up to 700m altitude.
lithdescript: Collected from bioclastic lenses 10-100cm thick, at the transition between lithozones 3 and 4 which partially interfinger in the lower-middle part of the Esimo Limestone, from 200-350m above the base to 500m below the of the formation. Lithozone 3 consists of bindstones, bafflestones and bio-intraclastic packstones and wackestones, whereas lithozone 4 consists of peloidal and bio-intraclastic packstones, wackestones, mudstones, and rarely grainstones.
geology_comments: Massive bioclastic limestones and patch reefs and prepresents the margin of Esino platform facing an intraplatform trough or an open basin to the south.
collection_comments: Collection donated to the Museo Civico de Scienze Naturali "E. Caffi" of Bergamo

lithdescript: The brachiopods described in this paper were collected from bioclastic lenses 10-100cm thick, at the transition between lithozones 3 and 4 which partially interfinger in the lower-middle part of the Esimo Limestone, from 200-350m above the base to 500m below the of the formation. collection_comments: Collection donated to the Museo Civico de Scienze Naturali "E. Caffi" of Bergamo

geogcomments: The Strzelc Opolskie Quarry provides one of the best exposures of the Muschelkalk deposits in Upper Silesia. Paleogeographically, this is the southern margin of the Germanic basin. The Muschelkalk Sea was connected with the Tethys Ocean to the south.
stratcomments: Middle Triassic/Lower Muschelkalk: The paleoecologic analysis is based on five sections from the Strzelc Opolskie Quarry. The five sections cover the entire span of the Terebratula Beds and the lowermost part of the Karchowice Beds. The Terebratula Beds are subdivided into three units: Lower marls, Crinoid limestones, and Coquina and wavy limestones (See lithological description below for details) Upper Silesian Region
lithdescript:
Lower marls - Crumpled and wavy limestones dominate in this unit. Shelly fossils are practically absent. Only in one place badly preserved tiny bivalves have been observed. 
Crinoid Limestone - Two firmgrounds occur in the lower part of this unit. the middle and upper parts are composed of thick calcarenitic beds. Dominant skeletal components change upward from mixed skeletal debris in the lower part, through crinoid columnals in the middle part, to terebratulid shell debis in the upper part. 
Coquinas and wavy limestone - Four lithological types have been distinguished: 
a) brachiopod coqunia. Up to 30 cm thick coquina layers, separated by crumpled and wavy limestone, occur in the whole unit. 
b) Crumpled and wavy limestone. Limestone beds which exhibit deformational structures varying from wavy bedding and gentle undulation, to structures intricately crumpled and fragmented. Fossils uncommon but their number increase upward.
c) Bivalve coquina. This lithology appears in the uppermost part if the unit as thin shell beds composed of closely packed internal molds of small articulated bivalves.
d) Organodetrial limestone with foraminifers. Numerous benthic forams are the main component of this limestone. 
Karchowice Beds - Crinoid and micritic limestones dominate in this unit. Sponges as well as brachiopods are identified. Very numerous are columnals of crinoids and in places, shells of unidentified bivalves. Hardgrounds with a rich assemblages of trace fossiles are well developed on the micritic limestone bedding planes
geology_comments: Brachiopod Coquina Assemblage - 38 bedding planes with 1598 specimens were classified as brachipod coquinas.

stratcomments: 8 feet above base of CCR section.\r\nGerster Formation is correlated with the upper Phosphoria Formation (Rex Chert, Retort, Tosi) and other upper units in the Park City Group (Franson, Ervay). Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

collection_name: USNM9266, Block 1, Khao Mang Lat Hill, Ban Kao
geogcomments: The Permian outcrop is on a hill called Khao Mang Lat about 45 minutes walk along the trail leading east from Ban Kao; Location based on lat/long of village of Ban Kao
stratcomments: The age of the Rat Buri fauna is problematic. "Rat Buri" limestones likely range in age from Kungurian through Capitanian to perhaps Wuchiapingian. Wordian fusulinids appear most common in other collections, but are not found in association with the brachiopod localities. The brachopod fauna is most similar to the Wordian Amb Formation of the Salt Range, in Pakistan, tentatively indicating a Wordian age.
lithdescript: Sandy silty limestone, with the maximum size of the sand in the medium range. Sand makes up about 10% of the rock and silt about 15%; the cement is calcite.
geology_comments: Depositional setting reconstructed as fairly shallow water, near shore and a source of terrigenous sediment, with a fairly firm substrate, in somewhat turbid water.
taxonomy_comments: Concentrates on brachiopods, accompanying faunas are mentioned but likely not fully described

collection_name: USNM9271, Block 1, Ko Muk Island northeast
geogcomments: Permian rocks make up much of the island, and are best exposed on high cliffs along the northeast and northwest side of the island, accessible only by sea, where fossil-bearing blocks can be collected from the base of the cliffs.
stratcomments: Blocks are derived from seacliffs, making it impossible to measure a stratigraphic section or determine whether they are derived from a single horizon. The age of the Rat Buri fauna is problematic. "Rat Buri" limestones likely range in age from Kungurian through Capitanian to perhaps Wuchiapingian. Wordian fusulinids appear most common in other collections, but are not found in association with the brachiopod localities. The brachopod fauna is most similar to the Wordian Amb Formation of the Salt Range, in Pakistan, tentatively indicating a Wordian age.
geology_comments: Interpreted as rather quiet water that was deep enough not to be disrupted by ordinary wave action. It was a fairly flat sea floor bearing an abundant fauna of small organisms with bryozoans and crinoids in patches like gardens.
taxonomy_comments: Concentrates on brachiopods, and other groups are listed only in the text for the generic total collection, not for the subset individual blocks.

stratcomments: Blocks are derived from seacliffs, making it impossible to measure a stratigraphic section or determine whether they are derived from a single horizon. The age of the Rat Buri fauna is problematic. "Rat Buri" limestones likely range in age from Kungurian through Capitanian to perhaps Wuchiapingian. Wordian fusulinids appear most common in other collections, but are not found in association with the brachiopod localities. The brachopod fauna is most similar to the Wordian Amb Formation of the Salt Range, in Pakistan, tentatively indicating a Wordian age.
geology_comments: Interpreted as rather quiet water that was deep enough not to be disrupted by ordinary wave action. It was a fairly flat sea floor bearing an abundant fauna of small organisms with bryozoans and crinoids in patches like gardens.
taxonomy_comments: Concentrates on brachiopods, and other groups are listed only in the text for the generic total collection, not for the subset individual blocks.

collection_name: Locality 1, Head of Quebrada de Portachuelo
geogcomments: Roughly 100 m downstream along Quebrada de Portachuelo (AKA Quebrada Queveda) from the highest redbed layer of the Sabaneta Formation.
stratcomments: A block of about 1 cubic m slipped into the streambed formed the actual site of collection. Fusulinids and ammonoids (Perrinites hilli) suggest that locality 4 (and underlying localities 1 and 2) are "late Leonardian" (Kungurian) in age.
lithdescript: Petroliferous, dark gray, fossiliferous, fissile siltstone, containing occasional lenses of silty limestone. Essentially a biomicrite although soft-sediment deformation created lenses of packstone.
geology_comments: Shallow, warm water of moderate current activity, probably below wave base. Abundant mud likely baffled by bryozoans but valve asymmetry in brachiopods suggests moderate current/wave activity.
preservation_comments: Fossils preserved entirely by calcite permineralization, and all were dark gray to black in color. Most fragments were crushed but rarely dispersed, suggesting post-depositional loading, not current or wave action. Little abrasion.
collection_comments: Fossils removed by hand from the weathered rock over an area of about 1 sq m, through a stratigraphic thickness of 0.5 m. Cleaned using S.S. White Airbrasive and other mechanical techniques.

Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age.
lithdescript: Petroliferous dark gray shale, with think (ca. 5 cm thick) intercalated lenses of clacerous siltstone. Biomicrite with soft-sediment deformation patches of wackestone or incipient packstone.
geology_comments: Shallow water with low energy, with a soft substrate. Absence of pediculate or cemented brachiopods suggests fine grain size and very soft substrates.
preservation_comments: Preserved by calcite permineralization and infilled by hydrocarbons. Most crushed (by post-depositional loading) but disarticulation was rare. Most disarticulated likely resulted from HF etching. No abrasion, suggesting authochthonous-parauthochthonous collection.
collection_comments: Size of area collected 1 m parallel to and 0.5 m normal to bedding. Fossils etched from siliceous shales with 52% hydrofluoric acid, which destroyed specimens over ~1 cm and decorticated smaller specimens.

geogcomments: Within the Quebrada de Portchuelo, about 100 m upstream from locality 3.
stratcomments: Area sampled is exposed in the side wall of the stream bed, and comprises about 2 m laterally and 1 m normal to bedding. Fusulinids and ammonoids suggest that locality 4 (and underlying localities 1 and 2) are "late Leonardian" (Kungurian) in age.  Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age.
lithdescript: Thin- to medium-bedded silty limestones, intercalated with thin-bedded calcareous siltstones. Compositionally a biomicrite, depositional texture classified as a packstone. Also contains silt- and sand-sized spherulites of possibly volcanic origin and fine needle-like calcitic forms interpreted as sponge spicules. Rip-up clasts present.
geology_comments: Graded bedding and fine sorting suggests periods of moderate to high energy, but the lack of abrasion and alternation of fine sediments suggests they were probably short-lived. Deposited in shallow, warm water, above a soft substrate.
preservation_comments: Fragmentation, poor preservation, and anomalous valve ratio of Meekella likely resulted from transportation (not poor silicification). Rip-up clasts also suggest storm influence. Reworked fossils likely lived nearby.
collection_comments: Sampled 2 m laterally and 1 m normal to bedding. Most were partially silicified (some totally silicified), etched with HCl. Dried silt periodically removed from block by air abrasion to speed decalcification.

collection_name: Locality 5, mule trail between El Portachuelo and Palo Quemado
geogcomments: About 1/4 the distance from El Portachuelo to Palo Quemado along mule trail.
stratcomments: Large (ca. 8 cubic meter) exotic block sampled for multiple blocks. Stratigraphic position unknown.  Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age.
lithdescript: Medium-gray, massive, petroliferous limestone. Compositionally a calcarenite, texture of a packstone. Silt-sized and clay-sized material present, as are rare dolomite rhombs.
geology_comments: Moderately good sorting of calcareous grains suggests a bar deposit. Abrasion and sorting also suggest high energy conditions. Absence of much terrigenous material suggests a bar, rather than beach, deposit. Dolomite may indicate slightly restricted conditions.
preservation_comments: Silicification is poor and partial. Most grains are not silicified. Larger silicified fossils are interpreted as being washed in from an outlying environment.
collection_comments: Etching only recovered a few fossils because of poor silicification. Cut slabs were also examined.

collection_name: Locality 6, Block A, mule trail between El Portachuelo and Mucuchachi
geogcomments: NA
stratcomments: Collected from bottom part of 2 cubic metre exotic block. Brachiopod similarities tentatively compared with Word Formation, but Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age.
lithdescript: Thick-bedded, petroliferous, light gray to tan silty limestones. Compositionally a spicular biomicrite; texturally a wackestone.
geology_comments: Shallow, warm water of moderate current activity. Lack of noticeable amounts of terrigenous material suggests low-relief coastline. Less restricted than locality 3, as dolomite rhombs are lacking.
collection_comments: Fossils obtained by hydrochloric acid etching.

collection_name: Capilla de la Santa Cruz de Palmarito, Locality 7
geogcomments: Paving stone in mule trail between Palo Quemado and Mucuchachi, about 1 km NW of Palo Quemado, 200 m toward Palo Quemado from the small chapel locally known as Capilla de la Santa Cruz de Palmarito.
stratcomments: Paving stone, could not be traced to outcrop; 1 m square and 25 cm thick.  Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age.
lithdescript: Dark gray, petroliferous, fossiliferous, very silty limestone. Heavily infiltrated by hydrocarbons. Sand and silt fractions display primitive sorting, with mm-scale graded beds. Compositionally a biomicrite containing sponge spicules and angular quartz and rock fragments. Soft-sediment deformation with recrystallization and intergranular welding. Texturally a packstone.
geology_comments: Shallow warm water, close to a shoreline of moderate relief (abundance of angular quartz fragments). Most breakage resulted from post-depositional compaction. Low abrasion and abundant micrite suggests low energy conditions.
preservation_comments: Only a few specimens are disarticulated.
collection_comments: 1 m square and 25 cm thick. Fossils identified from cut slabs.

collection_name: Capilla de la Santa Cruz de Palmarito, Locality 7
geogcomments: Paving stone in mule trail between Palo Quemado and Mucuchachi, about 1 km NW of Palo Quemado, 200 m toward Palo Quemado from the small chapel locally known as Capilla de la Santa Cruz de Palmarito.
stratcomments: Paving stone, could not be traced to outcrop; 1 m square and 25 cm thick.  Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age.
lithdescript: Dark gray, petroliferous, fossiliferous, very silty limestone. Heavily infiltrated by hydrocarbons. Sand and silt fractions display primitive sorting, with mm-scale graded beds. Compositionally a biomicrite containing sponge spicules and angular quartz and rock fragments. Soft-sediment deformation with recrystallization and intergranular welding. Texturally a packstone.
geology_comments: Shallow warm water, close to a shoreline of moderate relief (abundance of angular quartz fragments). Most breakage resulted from post-depositional compaction. Low abrasion and abundant micrite suggests low energy conditions.
preservation_comments: Only a few specimens are disarticulated.
collection_comments: 1 m square and 25 cm thick. Fossils identified from cut slabs.

geogcomments: Side wall of mule trail between Palo Quemado and Mucuchachi, 200 m toward Mucuchachi from the small chapel locally known as Capilla de la Santa Cruz de Palmarito.
stratcomments: Brachiopod similarities suggests equivalence to Road Canyon Fm (Kungurian-Roadian), Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age. 0.5 cubic metres sampled.

collection_name: Altamira House, Locality 10, Palo Quemado Trail
geogcomments: Along mule trail between El Portachuelo and Palo Quemado, in and on both sides of the trail itself, about 100 m S of house locally known as "Altamira"
lithdescript: Thin beds (5-15 cm) of slightly silty, dark gray limestone separated by thinner (ca. 1 cm) partings of gray siltstone. Texturally a wackestone.
geology_comments: Shallow, warm water below wave base, on a soft muddy bottom, with clear access to open ocean, and relatively far offshore. Low current activity (delicate structures are often preserved).
preservation_comments: Only a slightly disturbed living assemblage. Very little breakage or wear, extremely delicate structures are preserved.
collection_comments: Specimens from 2 m laterally and 1 m normal to bedding. Etched with HCL and dried silt residues removed by air abrasion.

collection_name: Locality 11, near head of Quebrada Palmar
geogcomments: Lying up a steep slope from a disused mule trail that connects El Portachuelo and Santa Rosa, on the west flank of Quebrada Palmar, near the head of that stream.
stratcomments: Several exotic blocks.  Palmarito Fm contains Perrinites hilli and Parafusulina of Kungurian age.
lithdescript: Thin- to medium-bedded, dense, dark gray, petroliferous fossiliferous silty packstone to grainstone and thinner, fossil-poor calcareous silstone. Limestone contains both relatively unfossiliferous biomicrite and very fossiliferous muddy calcarenite (packstone/grainstone).
geology_comments: Shallow, warm water, near wave base, over a soft substrate, in an area subject to periodic storms.
preservation_comments: Finely silicified but severely abraded in packstone layers. Possible transportation (based on valve distributions and abrasion), but possibly instead due to storm reworking. Fossil-rich layers interpreted as winnowed localized concentrations of derived from same environment.
collection_comments: Prepared by HCl etching, dried silt removed by air abrasion. Hustedia and Composita rare in calcareous siltstone, interpreted as generalist early colonizers.

geogcomments: La Democracia 1:50000 Quadrangle, near town of La Mesilla, 1 km N of Pan-American Highway. Intersection of map grid lines 11 (vertical) and 29 (horizontal).
stratcomments: Ammonoid, fusulinid, and brachiopod correlations suggest similarity to "Leonard" of West Texas, specifically Skinner Ranch, Cathedral Mountain, and Road Canyon (Artinskian-Roadian). Collected from a limestone lens in the lower part of the shaly beds, within the first 20 m above the main body of the Chochal Formation.
lithdescript: Consists primarily of thin-bedded, dark gray to black calcilutite but occasional thicker beds contain significant amounts of bioclastic debris and quartz silt though they are still very dark in color. Strongly deformed and often tightly folded.
geology_comments: Lithology description reminiscent of slope lithologies of Road Canyon Formation.
preservation_comments: Deformation has badly fractured and distorted much of the fossil material.
collection_comments: Several hundred pounds of limestone collected from both localities. geogcomments: Data from two 30 km spaced localities (not seperated in text)
40 km N of Mount Everest in southern Xizang (Tibet), 1 km NE of Shengmi village
stratcomments: Most likely of Wuchiapingian age, based on tentative brachiopod correlations, position immediately above Wuchiapingian flora in the underlying Qubu Formation, and position 200-300 m below late Changhsingian conodont Clarkina changxingensis. Lower member is 118.3 m thick.
lithdescript: Lower member is composed of muddy siltstone, and shale, and minor brown sandstone.
preservation_comments: Most of the brachiopods are represented by isolated valves and are poorly preserved with worn surfaces indicating that the shells were abraded during transportation prior to deposition.

collection_name: W1333, Section 18, Nangung Khola, Karnali (Nangung Fm)
geogcomments: Upstream of junction of Nangung Khola (River) and Panjang Khola.
stratcomments: Nangung Formation is correlated with the Kalabagh Member of the Salt Range based on brachiopods, which is Wuchiapingian in age. 12 m thick.
preservation_comments: Found principally as shells, and sometimes as weathered casts. No material has been silicified and much of it has been distorted under mountain building stress. Preservation is, on the whole, not very favourable.
collection_comments: Some collections were of individual specimens, others as large as possible under the circumstances, with a few localities represented by rock weighing more than 50 kg. Most collections were made from just over 50 measured sections, and are under good stratigraphic control.

geogcomments: The fossiliferous outcrops on the Oreg Hill near Vaszoly were discovered by I. Szabo and the first detailed collection made by the Hungarian Geological Survey was led also by him. The investigated section is located between Vaszoly and Pecsely villages and the Lake Balaton, on the gentle eastern slope of the Oreg Hill. 3 metres wide and 10 metres long trench, directed to SW–NE direction, was excavated in more than two metres depth, near the top of the Öreg Hill, in a grassy belt between two wooded areas (coordinates: x=46°55'45", y=17° 47'05").
stratcomments: Camunum subzone. Newly exposed trench reveals a sequence of about 6m in thickness, belonging to the Dorgicse Formation (somewhat equivalent of the formerly used "Buchenstein Beds" overlying the Anisian Megyehegy Dolomite Formation).
lithdescript: tuffaceous, calcerous sandstone, rich in ammonite and brachiopods
geology_comments: During the collection the bed numbers used by I Szabo were largely followed to avoid confusion, except for our interpretation for Bed 16/A.

geogcomments: The fossiliferous outcrops on the Oreg Hill near Vaszoly were discovered by I. Szabo and the first detailed collection made by the Hungarian Geological Survey was led also by him. The investigated section is located between Vaszoly and Pecsely villages and the Lake Balaton, on the gentle eastern slope of the Oreg Hill. 3 metres wide and 10 metres long trench, directed to SW–NE direction, was excavated in more than two metres depth, near the top of the Öreg Hill, in a grassy belt between two wooded areas (coordinates: x=46°55'45", y=17° 47'05").
stratcomments: Camunum subzone. Newly exposed trench reveals a sequence of about 6m in thickness, belonging to the Dorgicse Formation (somewhat equivalent of the formerly used "Buchenstein Beds" overlying the Anisian Megyehegy Dolomite Formation).
lithdescript: tuffaceous, calcerous sandstone, rich in ammonite and brachiopods
geology_comments: During the collection the bed numbers used by I Szabo were largely followed to avoid confusion, except for our interpretation for Bed 16/A.

collection_name: USNM702c, Old Word Ranch, Glass Mountains
geogcomments: From conical knob on S side of road at elbow just W of S branch of Hess Canyon, 4.5 miles by road NE of Hess gate, 1.35 miles S66.5W of Old Word Ranch and 4.03 miles N50E of Hess Ranch. Hess Canyon quadrangle.
stratcomments: Represents bioherms usually occurring at base of Road Canyon Formation. Lower part of Road Canyon Formation contains conodont Mesogondolella idahoensis lamberti, indicating Kungurian age according to Henderson & Mei (2003).
geology_comments: Road Canyon Formation records largely slope and basinal deposition.
taxonomy_comments: A variety of papers list the brachiopods, nearly all gastropods, most bivalves (except primarily Paleotaxodonts), trilobites, chitons, siliceous sponges, rugose corals (only from Gaptank and Asselian/Sakmarian formations).

geogcomments: The Horog-heny (265m) lies 2km ENE of the village of Köveskál, 4m N of northern shore of Lake Balaton. The fossiliferous localities occur on the forested northern slope of Horog-hegy, between the hilltop and an E-W running forest track.
stratcomments: The bulk of the hill is formed by Megyehegy Dolomite (lower Pelsonian?), overlain by gently dipping beds of Felsõörs Limestone (Pelsonian to Illyrian), about 40m in thickness.
lithdescript: Horog-hegy I: The lowermost unit is a more than 50 cm thick, light grey, slightly siliceous, unfossiliferous limestone (mudstone). This is overlain, with a sharp contact, by a 40cm thick, light brown, coarse-grained bioclastic limestone with brachiopods of rock-forming amount ("Upper Recaro")\r\nHorog-hegy II: a smaller, 2m wide outcrop around 50m eastward from the previous one, along the strike of the beds. The wxposed sequence is almost the same as in Horog-hegy I, but here the lowermost mudstone us well-bedded, slightly bituminous and yielded a poorly preserved Bulogites, and the brachiopod limestone ("Upper Recoaro") attains only 20 sm thickness.

geogcomments: Shore platform below Shot Tower at Taronga.  Grid reference EN278433.
stratcomments: Late Paleozoic fosiliferous marine sequence is almost everywhere subhorizontal and has a total thickness of about 675 meters. The late Lymingtonian (?Kazanian) assemblages described range throughout the uppermost 160 meters of this sequence in the Malbina Formation Member E and the overlying Risdon Sandstone and Abels Bay Formation and correlative beds. No measured section. Assigned to the Echinalosia hanloni/robusta zone by Briggs (1998), in the basal part of the APP4.2 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) placed the base of APP4.2 at 266.8 Ma, coincident with the base of the Wordian (266.9 Ma in Wu et al., 2020), so a Wordian age is assigned to these collections.
collection_comments: All fossils figured herein are deposited in the fossil collections of the Geological Survey of Tasmania (GST) or the Geology Department, University of Tasmania (UTGF).

geogcomments: Birchs Bay. Grid ref EN196187
stratcomments: Fossils occur throughout a few meters of section, but are concentrated in 38 cm thick bed. The Abels Bay Fm is the youngest marine Permian unit in Tasmanian, of late Lymingtonian age. Briggs (1998) correlated the late Lymingtonian with his mainland brachiopod zones, ranging from the Echinalosia wassi zone to the Echinalosia deari zone and with palynological zones APP4.3 and APP5. Radiometric calibration of these palynological zones by Laurie et al. (2016) suggests that APP4.3 is mid-Wuchiapingian and APP5 spans the late Wuchiapingian and Changhsingian. A Wuchiapingian age is assigned to the Abels Bay Formation here.\r\n
collection_comments: All fossils figured herein are deposited in the fossil collections of the Geological Survey of Tasmania (GST) or the Geology Department, University of Tasmania (UTGF).

Briggs (1998) correlated the late Lymingtonian with his mainland brachiopod zones, ranging from the Echinalosia wassi zone to the Echinalosia deari zone and with palynological zones APP4.3 and APP5. Radiometric calibration of these palynological zones by Laurie et al. (2016) suggests that APP4.3 is mid-Wuchiapingian and APP5 spans the late Wuchiapingian and Changhsingian. A Wuchiapingian age is assigned to the Abels Bay Formation here.\r\n

geogcomments: 1 km NW of the small village Selong, Nyalam County, S Tibet (Shen et al. 2000)
stratcomments: Equivalent to Bed 17 in Shen et al. (2000). The contact between the Selong Group and the overlying Kangshare Formation is marked by the Caliche Bed, a thin layer of pedogenic calcrete which varies laterally in thickness. The Kangshare Formation is 7.0 m thick and is divided into three beds (Jin et al., 1996): Waagenites Bed, Otoceras Bed, and Ophiceras Bed. The Otoceras and Ophiceras Beds are Triassic in age.
lithdescript: Bioclasts are finer in size and form around 35%, and sometimes less than 10%, of the rock. Bioclastics are usually well sorted, ranging from 0.5 mm to 2.0 mm in diameter. Packstone with poorly sorted bioclastics is also observed where the diameter of bioclastics may be up to 20 mm with slightly abraded unbroken crinoid stems. Contains greater amounts of ostracod and gastropod shells.\r\nJA: described by Shen et al. 2000 as a brown dolomitized crinoid packstone with brachiopods, corals, bryozoans, ostracods, foraminifers and calcareous sponges, above the "Caliche Bed", 0.07 m thick
geology_comments: This bed represents lag carbonate deposits formed in shallow, medium-energy shoal and in inter-shoal depressions.

collection_name: Lazurnaya Bay Fm (upper part) - South Primorye
geogcomments: GENERAL LOCATION: Exposures along eastern coast of Abrek Bay, near Krym, South Primorye, Russia. LAT/LONG: Estimate based on Fig. 1 (Zakharov and Shigeta 2000).
stratcomments: STRATIGRAPHIC RELATIONS: Lower Triassic strata in region are lithostratigraphically divided into the Lazurnaya Bay and Zhitkov Formations in an upward sequence. The Lazurnaya Bay Fm unconformably overlies the Permian Abrek Fm. THICKNESS: The Lazurnaya Bay Fm is 57.9 m thick in the Abrek Bay region. AGE: Contains an assemblage that suggest the lower Olenekian (lower part of the Hedenstroemia bisphorensis Zone) in the upper part of the formation, overlying upper Induan age sediments. The Induan/Olenekian boundary is located at 55 m above the base of the formation.
lithdescript: GENERAL LITHOLOGY: Gray, fine-grained, bedded sandstone, with lenses of coquinoid calcareous sandstone. LITHIFICATION: Lithified, based on observation of figured specimens.
geology_comments: ENVIRONMENT: No environmental data reported. Assigned to Siliciclastic coastal indet. on the basis of facies. TECTONIC SETTING: No tectonic data reported in text. SEQUENCE STRATIGRAPHY: No sequence stratigraphic data reported in text.
preservation_comments: TAPHONOMY: No taphonomic data reported in text.
collection_comments: COLLECTOR: Collection is a composite based on several workers, none of which are named. REPOSITORY: NSM (National Science Museum, Tokyo); CGM ?
taxonomy_comments: COMPLETENESS: Not exhaustive (as compiled from previous workers first hand accounts), but fairly complete. NOMENCLATURE: Authoritative text, modern nomenclature. Presumably nomenclature of taxa listed from older collections has been revised.

geogcomments: SPECIFIC LOCATION: Eastern wall of a cirque basin at the head of the southernmost branch of the Wilmot River, Skippers Range, northwest Otago, South Island, New zealand. MAPPING DATA: NZMS 260 Sheet D39, grid reference 249304. LAT/LONG: Converted Dec. Lat/Long44.43514°S 168.15911°E (NZGD49)
stratcomments: LITHOSTRATIGRAPHY: Mantle Volcanics Formation, within the Brook Street terrane. STRATIGRAPHIC POSITION: Mantle Volcanics Formation is 1300 m thick in this region and fossils were derived from talus boulders in the upper 600 m of the section. AGE: Assigned to the Sakmarian or possibly ?Sterlitamakian based on faunal composition. Previously regarded as Early Permian.
lithdescript: SPECIFIC LITHOLOGY: Very fine sand clinopyroxene and plagioclase crystal-lithic tuff, with isolated outsized lithic and lapilli clasts up to 20 mm in diameter. LITHIFICATION: Lithified, based on description and figured specimens.
geology_comments: ENVIRONMENT: Shall shelf, near wavebase, sands and silts, including taxa that tolerate rocky shoreline, proximal sandy shoreface, and distal sandy shoreface. TECTONIC SETTING: No tectonic data reported. SEQUENCE STRATIGRAPHY: No sequence stratigraphic data reported.
preservation_comments: SPECIFIC TAPHONOMY: Essentially a postmortem accumulation, but containing many double valved specimens and articulated crinoids. Some specimens are encrusted by bryozoans. Fossils preserved as recrystallised calcite in unweathered rock, but are leached to external and internal molds in weathered rock. Preservation is good, with fine surface features retained on many molds.
collection_comments: COLLECTOR: Collected by authors, J.G. Begg and H.R. Ballard, and C.A. Landis. REPOSITORY: Not stated, but almost definately the GNS (Geological Survey of New Zealand) or University of Otago.
taxonomy_comments: COMPLETENESS: Exhaustive for all taxa. NOMENCLATURE: Authoritative publication, with modern nomenclature.

geogcomments: Near Las Delicias, in the southwestern part of the State of Coahuila. Limestone lenses 25 meters east of El Indio.
lithdescript: Dark shale with nodular limestone beds a few inches thick and thin beds of graywacke (from section description, p. 13). Concretionary shale (From a general stratigraphy table, Fig. 3, p. 19).
geology_comments: The Permian rocks are folded in a syncline, and western limb is referred to as the Difunta flank. The strata in the Difunta flank dip to the east at an average angle of 45 degrees.

geogcomments: Near Las Delicias, in the southwestern part of the State of Coahuila. Limestone of Cerro Pichaguilla. geogcomments: Near Las Delicias, in the southwestern part of the State of Coahuila. Concretionary shale in area of complicated structure south-southeast of Cerro Prieto Norte. stratcomments: Part of middle Guadalupian (Cherry Canyon-Word) in west Texas and southeast New Mexico.
lithdescript: Shale and graywacke (from section description, p. 13). Prominent limestone layers separated from one another by shale, graywacke, and lava. Beds 11 to 17 and lower part of bed 10. Most imporant member is bed 15, which caps Cerro Caballo. Massive limestones have adundant sponges, crinoidal fragments; shales and thin limestones contain cephalopods. (From a general stratigraphy table, Fig. 3, p. 19).

The Difunta sections begins where the Arroyo la Difunta debouches from the hills east of Cerro San Pedro, and is measured westward to the Puerto de Sardinas, where the basal beds are overlapped by the Cretaceous.
lithdescript: Massive and nodular blue-gray limestone, with abundant Chonetes deliciaensis (from section description, p. 13). Prominent limestone layers separated from one another by shale, graywacke, and lava. Beds 11 to 17 and lower part of bed 10. Most imporant member is bed 15, which caps Cerro Caballo. Massive limestones have adundant sponges, crinoidal fragments; shales and thin limestones contain cephalopods. (From a general stratigraphy table, Fig. 3, p. 19).

geogcomments: Near Las Delicias, in the southwestern part of the State of Coahuila. Limestone lump 1150 meters S50W of Noria del Malascachas. The Malascachas section was measured from the lowest beds, which are exposed in a chain of hills about 2 kilometers southeast of the Noria de Malascachas, along the Arroyo Colorado and up the ridge west of Cerro Prieto Sur to the base of the Cretaceous escarpment about 1 kilometer west-southwest of the summit of Cerro Prieto Sur.
lithdescript: Blue-gray limestone with secondary chert, containing many sponges, corals, and crinoid stems (from section description, p. 10). Cephalopods abundant in shales (From a general stratigraphy table, Fig. 3, p. 19).

geogcomments: Haushi-Huqf Area. Five sections located in a small area between 21 00'37"N-57 39'35"E and 21 02'06"N-57 41'23"E, along the northwestern flank of the Haushi uplift. The Huqf area is located on the southeastern margin of the Arabian Plate, in the Sultanate of Oman.
stratcomments: Composite section built on five sections. Khuff is part of an unconformable second mega-sequence, which consists of the fluvial terrigenous Gharif Fm., overlain by marine marls and bioclastic limestones of the Khuff Fm.
geology_comments: This member is divided into two subunits. The lower subunit consists of cross-bedded, pebbly, bioclastic quartzarenites, and the overlying upper subunit consists of thin-bedded, cross-bedded, coarse to medium quartarenites alternating with bioclastic limestone. The lower subunit is interpreted as a barrier beach complex, and the upper subunit is interpreted as a mixed sand-mud shoreface environment.

geogcomments: NA
stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the lower Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlated with the upper APP3.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP3.1 zone does not have any radiometric constraints, although the top of the overlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Phillips et al. (2018) report ages of 282.72 and 282.41 Ma from strata no older than APP2.2, providing an upper constraint on APP3.1. Phillips et al. (2018) also place APP3.1 in the Kungurian, which is consistent with the presence of the ammonoid Neocrimites in APP3.1 of the Tiverton Formation (although not unequivocal).

collection_name: UQ L4108, Ross Creek Tributary, Cracow Station
geogcomments: NA
stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the Echinalosia discinia zone, correlated with the upper part of APP3.3 to APP4.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). There are no direct radiometric constraints on APP3.3, although the top of the underlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian. As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. The top of APP4.1 is likely late Wordian, constrained by earliest Capitanian radiometric dates in the lower part of APP4.2 (Laurie et al., 2016). The Broughton Formation, higher in the Sydney Basin succession, also yields an early Capitanian radiometric date (262.51 Ma) from its uppermost part, belonging to the upper part of APP4.2 (Metcalfe et al., 2015). Although the Brae Formation may extend to the Wordian, a Roadian age is assigned.

geogcomments: 12 miles east of Kamloops, BC, at Campbell Siding; north side of Thompson River
stratcomments: From upper part of unit. Nassichuk (1977) assigned an "early Guadalupian (Wordian)" age. It is possible, and perhaps more likely, that this collection is Roadian - the traditional Wordian encompasses the upper part of what is now formally defined as Roadian. The ammonoid Daubichites (although tentatively identified here) is characteristically Roadian, and Paraceltites and Waagenoceras both also occur in the upper Roadian in west Texas. Nelson & Nelson (1985) identified fusulinids that are early Guadalupian, and perhaps Wordian as Dunbarula laudoni co-occurs with Yabeina in its type area elsewhere. Limestone in the Harper Ranch Group spans a long age range based on conodonts (Orchard & Foster, 1988), including abundant Sakmarian-Kungurian ages. It is not clear whether the brachiopods and ammonoids were collected from the same beds or over the same age range.
geology_comments: environmental call is tentatively based on taphonomic/lithologic data provided; may be deep subtidal, but unlikely

lithdescript: 55 m of stratified fine grained bioclastic lime packstone with sponge spicules, crinoids, calcareous algae, and foraminifers, characterized by flat to round shaped cherts. Overlain by 10 m of grey nodular lime wackestone and then by 30 m of well bedded lime wackestone-packstone with marly interbeds.
taxonomy_comments: Only includes orthotetoid brachiopods - occasionally other fossils are mentioned in the text.

collection_name: AMNH631, Figure Two Ranch, Sierra Diablo
geogcomments: Immediately above the Hueco bioherm behind the Figure 2 ranch house, 2 miles south of Victorio Canyon.
stratcomments: The beds are believed to represent the very base of the Bone Spring formation on the shelf in this area.
lithdescript: The fossils are found in a relatively pure limestone, almost free of silt but containing abundant pebbles and great quantities of shell detritus which is badly\r\nworn and broken.
geology_comments: The bottom at the time of deposition was probably a coquina of broken shells in a lime matrix. The deposit was formed in very shallow water for it was the initial deposit above an unconformity. The water was probably less than 25 feet deep.

These constraints suggest a Wuchiapingian age for the Flat Top Formation.

As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian.

stratcomments: Near top of Wandrawandian Siltstone or base of Nowra Sandstone. Upper parts of the Wandrawandian Formation assigned to the Echinalosia discinia zone by Briggs (1998), although some Wandrawandian collections include brachiopods from the Echinalosia robusta/hanloni zone (the zone represented in the Nowra Formation). The upper E. discinia zone is correlated with the top of APP4.1 palynomorph zone, and the Echinalosia robusta/hanloni zone is correlated with APP4.2 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, indicating a late Roadian age. The APP4.2 zone was constrained as late Wordian to mid-Wuchiapingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). The E. robusta/hanloni zones are the basal part of APP4.2, so a Wordian age is assigned here.

In Main Range Creek, 0.8 km W of Bruce Highway, west of Collaroy in Nebo Synclinorium
stratcomments: Brachiopods indicate the Echinalosia provalis zone, correlated with the APP3.1 and lower APP3.2 palynomorph zones (Briggs, 1998). Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the top of APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age. The APP3.1 zone does not have any radiometric constraints, although the top of the overlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Phillips et al. (2018) place APP3.1 in the Kungurian, which is consistent with the presence of the ammonoid Neocrimites in APP3.1 of the the Tiverton Formation (although not unequivocal).

Although the Brae Formation may extend to the Wordian, a Roadian age is assigned.

Radiometric calibration of these palynologyical zones by Laurie et al. (2016) suggests that APP4.3 is mid-Wuchiapingian and APP5 spans the late Wuchiapingian and Changhsingian. stratcomments: 500 feet below top of Middle Bowen Marine Series, from the upper part of the Blenheim Subgroup (Dickins 1989). This part of the Blenheim Formation is Wuchiapingian in age, containing brachiopod zones correlated with the upper part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone or - more likely for this collection - lower part of APP5 (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age and APP5 as mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). However, overlying units in the Fort Cooper Coal Measures yield latest Wuchiapingian U-Pb ages (Phillips et al., 2018), constraining the upper Blenheim Fm to Wuchiapingian.

stratcomments: From the upper part of the stratigraphy containing the Big Strophalosia zone and clarkei bed. Upper part of the Blenheim Formation correlated with the upper part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone or lower part of APP5 (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age and APP5 as mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). However, overlying units in the Fort Cooper Coal Measures yield latest Wuchiapingian U-Pb ages (Phillips et al., 2018), constraining the upper Blenheim Fm to Wuchiapingian.

stratcomments: Glendoo Sandstone thought to be lateral equivalent of the middle part of the Gebbie Formation, most likely belonging to the upper Echinalosia maxwelli, E. davidi, or lower E. discinia brachiopod zones of Briggs (1998). These parts of the zones are correlated with the APP3.3 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the Rowan Formation in the Sydney Basin (in the underlying upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, or upper APP3.2) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian (Laurie et al. 2016). As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian.

stratcomments: Assigned to the Black Jack Formation (now considered a group), from a shallow marine facies underlying the Arkarula Sandstone member. In the Santos Brawboy 1 well, the Pamboola Formation underlies the Arkarula Fm, so the collection is assigned to the Pamboola Fm. In that well, the Pamboola Formation belongs to APP4.2-4.3 palynomorph zone, and is older than 257.33 Ma and younger than 262.54 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016). In the Santos Slacksmith 1 well, the Pamboola Fm is older than 258.05 Ma and younger than 264.75 Ma. Presence of Echinalosia denisoni suggests an age within the P. clarkei zone, correlated with the lower part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016).

stratcomments: Listed as "Upper Marine Series" in Fletcher (1943), but classic "Rylstone" collection comes from locality where "Capertee Formation" (correlative of the Snapper Point, according to Briggs, 1998) unconformably overlies Devonian. Brachiopods suggest the Echinalosia maxwelli brachiopod zone, equivalent to the upper part of APP3.2 or lower APP3.3 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the Rowan Formation in the Sydney Basin (in the underlying upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, or upper APP3.2) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian (Laurie et al. 2016). As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. As a result, the E. maxwelli zone is most likely Roadian.

stratcomments: Gebbie Formation assigned to the Echinalosia maxwelli, E. davidi, and E. discinia brachiopod zones of Briggs (1998). These zones are correlated with the APP3.3 palynomorph zone and APP4.1 for the upper E. discinia zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the Rowan Formation in the Sydney Basin (in the underlying upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, or upper APP3.2) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian (Laurie et al. 2016). As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. APP4.1 may extend into the Wordian, but a Roadian age is assigned to the formation.

stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the Echinalosia davidi or E. discinia zone, correlated with the upper part of APP3.3 to APP4.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). There are no direct radiometric constraints on APP3.3, although the top of the underlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian. As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. The top of APP4.1 is likely late Wordian, constrained by earliest Capitanian radiometric dates in the lower part of APP4.2 (Laurie et al., 2016). The Broughton Formation, higher in the Sydney Basin succession, also yields an early Capitanian radiometric date (262.51 Ma) from its uppermost part (Metcalfe et al., 2015). Therefore upper parts of the formation are possibly early Wordian in age, but a Roadian age is assigned in the Ulladulla area.
geology_comments: Fine-grained sediments indicate environment below wave base, and presence of slumps at Warden Head suggests prodelta rather than offshore.

geogcomments: NA
lithdescript: Fine-grained, slightly muddy sandstone is predominant in the remainder of Interval 3 (820.5-862.5 m), and is associated with a few mudstone beds. Pebbles are scattered throughout the sequence. The sandstones are moderately to well sorted, and occur in beds ranging in thickness from 0.6 to 9.5 m. Mudstone beds are up to 1.6 m thick. Three upward fining sandstones with erosional bases and sharp upper boundaries are present; one of the beds passes upwards into mudstone. The uniform sandstones are bioturbated throughout, although bioturbation is less extensive in the uppermost sandstone where some lamination is preserved. The upward fining beds exhibit a consistent vertical sequence of sedimentary structures; laminae and cross-laminae are present in the lower part and bioturbation is restricted to the upper part. Mudclasts are present near the base of one of these sandstones. Burrows are vertical or oblique and are generally filled with mudstone. Mudstone beds are only moderately bioturbated and contain numerous lenticular or irregular sandstones, which are laminated or ripple cross-laminated. Soft sediment deformation structures are common.  Carbonaceous laminae and patches of finely divided plant material are present in the upward fining beds.
geology_comments: The predominance of fine sandstone, the abundance of burrows, and the presence of a few fossiliferous beds suggest relatively slow sedimentation in a nearshore environment. The high proportion of sand suggests that sedimentation was affected by periodic wave or current activity, but sedimentation rates were sufficiently low to allow bioturbation and the obliteration of most primary sedimentary structures. Common fine plant material suggests proximity to the shoreline and, as discussed in the preceding section, the presence of scattered pebbles throughout the sequence suggests open marine conditions.

Mudstone beds are only moderately bioturbated and contain numerous lenticular or irregular sandstones, which are laminated or ripple cross-laminated. Soft sediment deformation structures are common.  Carbonaceous laminae and patches of finely divided plant material are present in the upward fining beds.
geology_comments: The predominance of fine sandstone, the abundance of burrows, and the presence of a few fossiliferous beds suggest relatively slow sedimentation in a nearshore environment. The high proportion of sand suggests that sedimentation was affected by periodic wave or current activity, but sedimentation rates were sufficiently low to allow bioturbation and the obliteration of most primary sedimentary structures. Common fine plant material suggests proximity to the shoreline and, as discussed in the preceding section, the presence of scattered pebbles throughout the sequence suggests open marine conditions.

stratcomments: Presence of Echinalosia preovalis indicates the E. provalis zone, correlated with the APP3.1 and lower APP3.2 palynomorph zones (Briggs, 1998). Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the top of APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age. The APP3.1 zone does not have any radiometric constraints, although the top of the overlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Phillips et al. (2018) place APP3.1 in the Kungurian, which is consistent with the presence of the ammonoid Neocrimites in APP3.1 of the the Tiverton Formation (although not unequivocal).

stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the Echinalosia maxwelli brachiopod zone, equivalent to the upper part of APP3.2 or lower APP3.3 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the top of APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age, which is used here.

stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the E. discinia zone, correlated with the upper part of APP3.3 to APP4.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). There are no direct radiometric constraints on APP3.3, although the top of the underlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian. As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. The top of APP4.1 is likely late Wordian, constrained by earliest Capitanian radiometric dates in the lower part of APP4.2 (Laurie et al., 2016). The Broughton Formation, higher in the Sydney Basin succession, also yields an early Capitanian radiometric date (262.51 Ma) from its uppermost part (Metcalfe et al., 2015). Therefore upper parts of the formation are possibly early Wordian in age.

stratcomments: Basal E. maxwelli Zone correlative, or older. S. yalwalensis is known only from the basal Snapper Point Formation in the Yalwal area. where it overlies pre·Permian basement. Elsewhere in the southern Sydney Basin the Snapper Point Formation is a correlative of the Echinalosia maxwelli Zone, but the fossiliferous basal unit at Yalwal could be an erosional remnant of an older formation. Echinalosia maxwelli brachiopod zone is equivalent to the upper part of APP3.2 or lower APP3.3 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the Rowan Formation in the Sydney Basin (in the underlying upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, or upper APP3.2) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian (Laurie et al. 2016). As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. As a result, the E. maxwelli zone is most likely Roadian.

(2018) report ages of 282.72 and 282.41 Ma from strata no older than APP2.2, suggesting that the upper parts of APP3.1 are most likely Kungurian.

stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the Echinalosia maxwelli brachiopod zone, equivalent to the upper part of APP3.2 or lower APP3.3 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the top of APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age, which is used here.

The top of APP4.1 is likely late Wordian, constrained by earliest Capitanian radiometric dates in the lower part of APP4.2 (Laurie et al., 2016). The Broughton Formation, higher in the Sydney Basin succession, also yields an early Capitanian radiometric date (262.51 Ma) from its uppermost part, belonging to the upper part of APP4.2 (Metcalfe et al., 2015). stratcomments: From basal few metres of formation. Brachiopods indicate the upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlated with the lower APP3.2 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the top of APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age.

stratcomments: Basal E. maxwelli Zone correlative, or older. S. yalwalensis is known only from the basal Snapper Point Formation in the Yalwal area. where it overlies pre·Permian basement. stratcomments: "Probably near the base of the Middle Bowen Beds." The lower Middle Bowen Beds is equivalent to the Gebbie Formation in the Nebo Synclinorum, including the Wall Sandstone (marked by Dickins et al. 1964 at the base of the Middle Bowen). The Wall Sandstone was assigned to the top of the Echinalosia preovalis (upper) brachiopod zone, equivalent to the middle part of APP3.2 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from an equivalent position within APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age. However, the Wall Sandstone is from the upper part and is possibly Roadian. It is also possible that the specimen comes from the Gebbie Formation excluding the Wall Sandstone, so a Roadian age is assigned.

stratcomments: Lower 50-60 feet of unit.\r\nBrachiopods indicate the Echinalosia davidi zone, correlated with the APP3.3 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). There are no direct radiometric constraints on APP3.3, although the top of the underlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian. As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian.

collection_name: Rathbone's Quarry, Rayner Creek, Mount Nassau
geogcomments: Outcrop between Rayner and Geiss creeks
stratcomments: Berriedale Limestone assigned to the lower Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlative with the upper part of palynomorph zone APP3.1 by Briggs (1998). The APP3.1 zone does not have any radiometric constraints, although the top of the overlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Phillips et al. (2018) report ages of 282.72 and 282.41 Ma from strata no older than APP2.2, providing an upper constraint on APP3.1. Phillips et al. (2018) also place APP3.1 in the Kungurian, which is consistent with the presence of the ammonoid Neocrimites in APP3.1 of the the Tiverton Formation (although not unequivocal). It is possible that the formation may span the Artinskian-Kungurian boundary.

geogcomments: Cuttings beside the track to the Hobart City Council reservoir.
stratcomments: Horizon B. About 45 m below the top of the group.\r\nThe Ferntree Fm is the youngest marine Permian unit in Tasmanian, of late Lymingtonian age. Briggs (1998) correlated the late Lymingtonian with his mainland brachiopod zones, ranging from the Echinalosia wassi zone to the Echinalosia deari zone and with palynological zones APP4.3 and APP5. Radiometric calibration of these palynologyical zones by Laurie et al. (2016) suggests that APP4.3 is mid-Wuchiapingian and APP5 spans the late Wuchiapingian and Changhsingian. A Wuchiapingian age is assigned to the Ferntree Formation here.

Section measured from Yinshangpo to Sizishan, in the vicinity of Qingyan, a small town 25 km S of Guiyang, the capital of Guizhou Province.
stratcomments: Bed 4 (units KC 259-262) is 80 m thick. About 200 m above base of Qingyan Formation.
lithdescript: Qingyan Formation consists mainly of gray to yellowish-green noncalcareous shale, pale-to dark-gray marl, calcareous shale, and argillaceous limestone, usually thin-bedded. Most of the fossils are collected from the shale and marl.
geology_comments: Evaporative basin in Sichuan and north Guizhou separated from open marine to south in Yunnan and Guangxi by biohermal belt, located just north of Qingyan. The area near Qingyan was a prebiohermal facies. (Apparently fore-reef or something equivalent, located on the slope?)

lithdescript: Qingyan Formation consists mainly of gray to yellowish-green noncalcareous shale, pale-to dark-gray marl, calcareous shale, and argillaceous limestone, usually thin-bedded. Most of the fossils are collected from the shale and marl.
geology_comments: Evaporative basin in Sichuan and north Guizhou separated from open marine to south in Yunnan and Guangxi by biohermal belt, located just north of Qingyan. The area near Qingyan was a prebiohermal facies. (Apparently fore-reef or something equivalent, located on the slope?)

collection_name: Hatahoko, Yokoberadani Valley, Nyukawa-machi, Takayama City
geogcomments: Lower part of a large limestone block exposed over a 4 by 0.5 km area, 500 m thick, in the Middle Jurassic Hirayu Complex. The sampling locality is located at the upper Yokoberadani Valley, Hatahoko, Nyukawa-machi, Takayama City, Gifu Prefecture
stratcomments: The conodont fauna includes abundant Sweetognathus guizhouensis Bando et al., 1982, associated with Pseudohindeodus augustus (Igo, 1981), and no gondolellid species. Sweetognathus guizhouensis has been reported from the lower and middle parts of the Chihsia Formation of Guizhou, South China, which is approximately correlated with the lower to middle Kungurian (Bando et al., 1982; Ding and Xia, 1996; Henderson and Mei, 2003; Mei et al., 2002) and the Kungurian equivalents in southeast Pamir and Sicily (Henderson and Mei, 2003; Kozur, 1993; Reimers, 1991). Pseudohindeodus augustus has been reported from the Sakmarian to Kungurian Akuda and Kuchibora formations in Gujohachiman, Gifu Prefecture, central Japan (Igo, 1981) and the Bolorian Neostreptognathodus sulcoplicatus Zone in Pamir (Reimers, 1999).
geology_comments: Relatively quiet environment slightly below wave base dominated by soft substrate on a Panthalassan seamount.
preservation_comments: Silicification is not explicitly stated, but fossils were extracted from limestone with 2-5% formic acid.

lithdescript: The uppermost Permian comprises bioclastic limestone of the Changhsing Formation.  This formation is capped by a thin layer of dark muddy limestone (Bed 19) rich in trace fossil Chondrites ichnosp. The possible P/Tr mass extinction horizon is calibrated to the base of Bed 19 by the first occurrence of the conodont N. meishanensis
preservation_comments: Preservation is variable; brachiopod specimens comprise shells, whereas both ammonoids and bivalves are moulds and crinoids are represented by inarticulated stems, bryozoans by fragmented branches, and fossil fishes by fragmented scales.
collection_comments: recovered from the surfaces of mudstone or marlstone or limestone slabs, forming total areas of 0.2 to 0.3 m2 for each sample. all of bryozoans, crinoids and fishes are excluded from quantitative analysis.

collection_name: UNE L845, Pacific Highway, Raymond Terrace
geogcomments: Road cutting on Pacific Highway 5.5 km N of Raymond Terrace. (Paterson 1:63,360). NEWCASTLE[yd] 4803 9541
stratcomments: 845/1 from 20 m above base of unit. 845/ 2 from 8 m higher in sequence, within plant bed. 845/3 from 10 m higher. 845M includes loose material. Brachiopods indicate the upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlated with the lower APP3.2 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the top of APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age.

geogcomments: In paddock to south of eastern end of second cutting west of minor overhead bridge.  From south side of railway cutting (second west of minor bridge over line), from just within paddock (Singleton 1:63,360). SINGLETON[yd] 4296 9624
stratcomments: Formation belongs to the Echinalosia davidi brachiopod zone, equivalent to the middle part of APP3.3 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the Rowan Formation in the Sydney Basin (in the underlying upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, or upper APP3.2) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian (Laurie et al. 2016). As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. As a result, the E. davidi zone is most likely Roadian.

stratcomments: Formation correlated with the upper part of APP3.3 to APP4.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). There are no direct radiometric constraints on APP3.3, although the top of the underlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian. As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. The top of APP4.1 is likely late Wordian, constrained by earliest Capitanian radiometric dates in the lower part of APP4.2 (Laurie et al., 2016). The Broughton Formation, higher in the Sydney Basin succession, also yields an early Capitanian radiometric date (262.51 Ma) from its uppermost part (Metcalfe et al., 2015).

collection_name: UNE L845, Pacific Highway, Raymond Terrace
geogcomments: Road cutting on Pacific Highway 5.5 km N of Raymond Terrace. (Paterson 1:63,360). NEWCASTLE[yd] 4803 9541
stratcomments: 845/1 from 20 m above base of unit. 845/ 2 from 8 m higher in sequence, within plant bed. 845/3 from 10 m higher. 845M includes loose material. Brachiopods indicate the upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlated with the lower APP3.2 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the top of APP3.2 (Rowan Formation) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). The base of APP3.2 is not constrained radiometrically, so it is unclear whether the zone is entirely Roadian or extends down to the Kungurian. The base of the Roadian is also unclear. Wu et al. (2017) argued for an age close to 272.95 Ma based on zircons from South China just below the local first occurrence of J. nankingensis. However, Davydov et al. (2018) obtained U-Pb dates of 273.1 and 274.0 Ma from units bearing ammonoids typically assigned to the Roadian in boreal regions, and argued for the base of the Roadian as old as 277 Ma. If the base of the Roadian is the younger date, then APP3.2 may largely be Kungurian in age.

geogcomments: GR 352932, Monto 1:250 000 sheet. Por. 18, Par. Prospect, in upper part of Scoria Creek
stratcomments: Brachiopods from nearby localities in the unit suggest the lower Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlated with the upper APP3.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the lower Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlated with the upper APP3.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP3.1 zone does not have any radiometric constraints, although the top of the overlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Phillips et al. (2018) report ages of 282.72 and 282.41 Ma from strata no older than APP2.2, providing an upper constraint on APP3.1. Phillips et al. (2018) also place APP3.1 in the Kungurian, which is consistent with the presence of the ammonoid Neocrimites in APP3.1 of the Tiverton Formation (although not unequivocal).

lithdescript:
"Unit K3/kz1   Interval 0.00-0.10m   Thickness (visible) 0.10m
Shale: brown to brownish grey, with numerous crushed brachiopods... and numerous fragments of bryozoans and crinoids. The shell structure is well preserved.
Unit K3/kz2   Interval 0.10-0.55m   Thickness 0.45m
Limestone: pale grey, argillaceous, fine-grained, bedded, with disrupted subparallel sedimentary lamination. The lamination is also expressed on polished slabs as predominant horizontal orientation of bioclasts that locally imbricate to form "micro-pavements". Lamination planes show plant detritus, charophyte stalks, sparse Cancrinella, and unidentified branching calcareous microtubules. The rock is microporous, soft, and waterlogged at 0.30-0.45m of cumulative thickness.
Unit K3/kz3   Interval 0.55-0.85m   Thickness 0.30m
Limestone: grey, weathers brownish, micritic (bioclastic wackestone to mudstone), weakly fissile, probably weakly argillaceous, with numerous Cancrinella on the bedding planes in the middle. Randomly oriented bioclasts indicate bioturbation. Bioclastic micro-pavements are locally preserved in the middle part of the unit.
Unit K3/kz4   Interval 0.85-1.35m   Thickness 0.5m
Calcareous marl: dark grey, weathers brownish, unevenly hard, moderately fissile, laterally grading to the soft marly rock. Bioturbated bioclastic wackestone or calcimudstone with rare patches of bioclast micro-pavements.
Unit K3/kz5   Interval 1.35-1.45m   Thickness 0.10m
Limestone: pale brownish grey, dolomitic, fine-grained, thin-bedded. Base conformable and gradational. This unit may be a part of the 'Chervotochina' Bed sensu Noinsky (1899, 1924). This unit can be described as a transition from fissile marl K3/kz4 to thick-bedded dolostone K3/1 marking a conformable contact of the Lower and Upper Kazanian in the type section." (Nurgaliev et al. 2015)

A large group of isolated limestone blocks from meter to kilometer scale are located in the Mesozoic deposits in the Zhongbei–Qianggong area in the Lhaze County, about 300 km west of Lhasa, the capital city of Tibet.  The fossils described in this paper were collected from the largest one in the Quxia limestone, which likely represents the lower and middle part of the Quxia limestone. A small village called Xiukang is situated to the west about 400 m from the block.
stratcomments: Association with Timorites and presence of Urushtenoidea suggests Capitanian age.

stratcomments: Brachiopods from the area suggest the upper Echinalosia maxwelli or E. davidi zone, correlated with the APP3.3 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). There are no direct radiometric constraints on APP3.3, although the top of the underlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian. As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian.

geogcomments: In a quarry, 1 mile west-north-west of Mulbring, 16 miles west of Newcastle, at 475336 Cessnock 1:63,360 military map
stratcomments: Brachiopods from the formation suggest the Echinalosia davidi brachiopod zone, equivalent to the middle part of APP3.3 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the Rowan Formation in the Sydney Basin (in the underlying upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, or upper APP3.2) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian (Laurie et al. 2016). As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. As a result, the E. davidi zone is most likely Roadian.

collection_name: UQ L4822, Buffel Hill, Cracow Homestead
geogcomments: NA
stratcomments: Brachiopods suggest the lower Echinalosia preovalis zone, correlated with the upper APP3.1 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP3.1 zone does not have any radiometric constraints, although the top of the overlying APP3.2 is around 271.6 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016), placing it near the Kungurian-Roadian boundary or in the lower Roadian. Phillips et al. (2018) report ages of 282.72 and 282.41 Ma from strata no older than APP2.2, providing an upper constraint on APP3.1. Phillips et al. (2018) also place APP3.1 in the Kungurian, which is consistent with the presence of the ammonoid Neocrimites in APP3.1 of the Tiverton Formation (although not unequivocal).

stratcomments: "Ulladulla Formation." From lower Wandrawandian Formation, Echinalosia maxwelli and E. davidi zone correlative. Upper Echinalosia maxwelli or E. davidi brachiopod zones are equivalent to the middle of the APP3.3 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). Laurie et al. (2016) dated zircons from the Rowan Formation in the Sydney Basin (in the underlying upper Echinalosia preovalis zone, or upper APP3.2) as 271.60 and 271.89 Ma, constraining its upper part to Roadian, given a Roadian-Wordian boundary around 266.9 Ma (Wu et al., 2020). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, constraining the upper boundary of APP3.3 to the late Roadian (Laurie et al. 2016). As a result, APP3.3 appears to fall entirely within the Roadian. As a result, the locality is most likely Roadian.
